messages.subject: Re: brain registration
parts:
Dear Emilia,

Unfortunately the Stanford server died and couldn't be replaced at that address. The new location for information / downloads for the registration tools is:

http://flybrain.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/dokuwiki/doku.php?id=warping_manual:start

We actually now recommend saving input images in nrrd format according to the instructions at

http://flybrain.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/dokuwiki/doku.php?id=warping_manual:registration_gui

The relevant plugins are bundled with Fiji by default and can be accessed by File ... Save as ... Nrrd

Incidentally if you look at the bottom of the page you will see a download for the classic macosx gui, although we now recommend the CMTK registration plugin that you have already installed.

Best wishes,

Greg Jefferis.

PS I have taken the liberty of ccing this message to the nat-user google group since the answer may be of interest to others.

messages.subject: Re: brain registration
parts:
Dear Emilia,

This warning is harmless – the registration is running normally. What
it is saying is that there is no anatomical orientation data embedded in
the image that can be used automatically to put the image data into a
standard orientation.

For example when human brain images are acquired in an MRI scanner, the
axes of the image data are tagged with appropriate anatomical axes.
However no confocal software currently enables this, so you must ensure
that your image data is saved so that the image x,y,z dimensions
consistently match those for the template image. If this is not the
case, then you would need to specify an initial registration that
re-orients the sample image appropriately or pre-process the sample
images to ensure that they are appropriately rotated etc.

Best wishes,

Greg.

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: brain registration
parts:
> Thanks-- I have an additional question; I am running the registration
> but only getting the NC82 channel back in the reformatted folder. I
> don't see any image with the second channel, which is a GFP-stained
> Gal4 line. Am I missing something? I set the NC82 channel to be
> _01.nrrd, which is what I understood from the instructions. But how do
> I get and re-merge the additional channel?

Does your input "images" folder also contain the second channel? It
should look like this:

images/mybrain_01.nrrd
images/mybrain_02.nrrd

Notice that it is very important that

1. the file stem ("mybrain") in the above example is consistent between
the two images.
2. the files for each channel end in "_01.nrrd" and "_02.nrrd"

Best,

Greg.
